title: Monitor, Triage and Keep It Accurate
brief: Given a Monitor export of Meridian conversations with user feedback, produce a triage
sheet: root cause, the correct fix LAYER, owner, priority. Then fix the top five.
The layer is the whole point. The same wrong answer can be a data problem, a knowledge
store gap, a missing example query, or a question nobody could answer. Fixing it in the
wrong layer works once and rots, because the next question phrased differently breaks
again. Prose that patches a data problem is the most common version of this mistake.
review: Every row names a layer, not just a fix.
At least one item is correctly triaged as 'the data is wrong', not an agent problem.
At least one is correctly closed as expected behaviour rather than a defect.
Priorities reflect how many people hit the issue, not how annoying it was to whoever reported it.
